merger_name: Sims - business assets of Base Metal Recyclers, VIC

anzsic_codes.name: Waste Remediation and Materials Recovery Services

merger_description:
Sims Group Australia Holdings Limited (**SGAHL**), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Sims Limited (**Sims**), proposes to acquire the business and operating assets of Base Metal Recyclers (**Base Metal**) from PPM Industries Pty Ltd as trustee of the PPM Industries Unit Trust (the **Acquisition**).

Sims operates scrap metal recycling facilities across Australia. In the greater Melbourne area, Sims operates facilities at Brooklyn, Broadmeadows and Noble Park. Sims also operates facilities in Geelong and Traralgon in Victoria.

Base Metal Recyclers operates a scrap metal recycling business at 14 Sigma Drive, Croydon South, Victoria.

The assets to be acquired comprise the operating business conducted by Base Metal, including its Croydon South site, together with plant and equipment, motor vehicles, inventory, business contracts, intellectual property, business name, goodwill and other assets associated with the Base Metal Recyclers business.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. while there is horizontal overlap between Sims and Base
Metal in the acquisition of ferrous and non-ferrous scrap
metal and the supply of processed ferrous and non-ferrous
scrap metal in Victoria, the incremental share arising from
the Acquisition would be small
b. there are alternative acquirers of ferrous and non-ferrous
scrap metal and suppliers of processed ferrous and non-
ferrous scrap metal in Victoria.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
